rows.label: cassava
rows.description: species of plant native to South America cultivated for industrial and food uses
rows.hook: is a starchy root crop turned into flour, chips, and tapioca pearls across the tropics

rows.label: Persea americana
rows.description: species of plant, use Q961769 for the fruit
rows.hook: is a tree grown for its buttery green flesh, essential to guacamole and toast

rows.label: maize
rows.description: species of grass cultivated as a food crop
rows.hook: is a towering grass whose golden cobs are a staple food worldwide

rows.label: potato
rows.description: species of plant (for the food, use Q16587531)
rows.hook: is an underground tuber that became a staple crop across Europe after arriving from the Andes

rows.label: Citrus × limon
rows.hook: is a sour yellow orchard crop whose juice and zest flavor drinks and desserts

rows.label: Hibiscus
rows.hook: is a genus of large, trumpet-shaped tropical blooms often dried into tea

rows.label: peanut
rows.description: legume cultivated for use of the underground seedpods as a grain crop, and also processed as peanut oil
rows.hook: grows its seedpods underground and is pressed into a popular cooking oil

rows.label: Chrysanthemum
rows.hook: is a many-petaled autumn bloom central to East Asian festivals and tea

rows.label: Ficus carica
rows.hook: is a Mediterranean tree whose soft, seed-filled treat is dried for snacking

rows.label: sweet potato
rows.hook: is an orange-fleshed root crop baked into pies and fries around the world

rows.label: date palm
rows.description: palm tree cultivated for its edible sweet fruit
rows.hook: is a desert tree bearing a sticky, sugar-rich delicacy eaten dried

rows.label: Curcuma longa
rows.hook: is a golden-rooted plant that colors curry dishes and gives mustard its hue

rows.label: Ananas comosus
rows.hook: is a spiky tropical treat crowned with a leafy tuft and tangy golden flesh

rows.label: black pepper
rows.hook: is a tropical vine whose dried berries are ground into the world's most common table seasoning

rows.label: Hordeum vulgare
rows.hook: is a cereal crop malted to brew beer and whisky

rows.label: Avena sativa
rows.hook: is a cereal crop rolled into breakfast porridge and hearty granola bars

rows.label: strawberry
rows.description: hybrid species in the rose family
rows.hook: is a heart-shaped red treat with its seeds dotting the outside

rows.label: watermelon
rows.hook: is a summer favorite with sweet pink flesh and a rind used for pickling

rows.label: soybean
rows.description: species of plant in the Fabaceae family
rows.hook: is a protein-rich crop pressed into oil, milk, and blocks of tofu

rows.label: Rosa
rows.hook: is a thorny-stemmed bloom long given as a symbol of romance

rows.label: Lilium
rows.hook: is a trumpet-shaped bloom whose scent fills funerals and Easter services

rows.label: broccoli
rows.description: edible green plant in the cabbage family
rows.hook: is a tree-shaped green crop packed into stir-fries and steamed side dishes

rows.label: Dionaea muscipula
rows.hook: snaps its hinged leaves shut to trap and digest unlucky insects

rows.label: Cucumis sativus
rows.description: species of plant in the Cucurbitaceae family
rows.hook: is a cool, watery crop sliced into salads and pickled into jars

rows.label: Nelumbo nucifera
rows.hook: rises unstained from muddy ponds as a symbol of purity in Asian religions

rows.label: Camellia sinensis
rows.hook: is the shrub whose picked leaves are dried and steeped to brew a global favorite drink

rows.label: Prunus persica
rows.description: species of fruit tree (for the fruit use Q13202263)
rows.hook: is a fuzzy-skinned orchard treat with sweet golden flesh around a hard pit

rows.label: common sunflower
rows.description: species of flowering plant in the family of Asteraceae
rows.hook: turns its tall golden head to track the sun across the sky

rows.label: ginger
rows.hook: is a knobby root grated into stir-fries and steeped for a soothing tea

rows.label: Sequoiadendron giganteum
rows.description: species of tree native to North America
rows.hook: is the world's most massive living thing, towering over California's mountains

rows.label: Bambusoideae
rows.hook: shoots upward nearly a meter in a single day and feeds giant pandas

rows.label: Papaver somniferum
rows.hook: produces the sap used to make morphine, and its tiny seeds top bagels

rows.label: Dahlia
rows.hook: is Mexico's national bloom, prized by gardeners for its geometric petal spirals

rows.label: Capsicum annuum
rows.description: species of the plant genus Capsicum
rows.hook: ranges from sweet bell varieties to fiery chilies that bring the heat to salsas

rows.label: Aloe vera
rows.hook: stores soothing gel in its thick spiky leaves, popular for sunburn relief

rows.label: basil
rows.hook: is the fragrant leaf at the heart of pesto and classic Italian cooking

rows.label: Jasminum
rows.description: genus of plants in the Oleaceae family
rows.hook: releases a heady evening scent prized in perfumes and scented teas

rows.label: Narcissus
rows.description: genus of plants in family Amaryllidaceae
rows.hook: pushes up trumpet-shaped yellow blooms as one of spring's first signs

rows.label: Tulipa
rows.hook: sparked a speculative bulb-trading frenzy in the Dutch Golden Age

rows.label: Carnegiea gigantea
rows.hook: lives up to two centuries, raising arm-like limbs across the Arizona desert

rows.label: Paeonia
rows.hook: unfurls huge ruffled blooms long grown in Chinese imperial gardens

rows.label: Sequoia sempervirens
rows.description: species of plant in the monotypic genus Sequoia in the cypress family (Cupressaceae)
rows.hook: is the tallest living thing on Earth, soaring above California's foggy coast

rows.label: Tagetes
rows.hook: lines gardens in fiery orange and gold and honors the dead on Dia de los Muertos

rows.label: Cannabis sativa
rows.hook: yields tough fibers once spun into rope and sails for centuries of sailors

rows.label: Lavandula
rows.hook: perfumes fields of Provence with its purple spikes and calming scent

rows.label: Lactuca sativa
rows.hook: forms crisp leafy heads that anchor salads and sandwiches worldwide

rows.label: cacao
rows.description: tree native to tropical South America producing cocoa beans - the source plant of cacao and chocolate
rows.hook: grows pods on its trunk whose bitter beans are roasted into chocolate

rows.label: Iris
rows.description: genus of plants in the order Iridaceae
rows.hook: displays three drooping petals in a shape inspiring France's fleur-de-lis

rows.label: Dianthus caryophyllus
rows.hook: grows ruffled, clove-scented petals worn as a classic boutonniere

rows.label: Bellis perennis
rows.description: Flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae
rows.hook: dots lawns with white petals ringing a cheerful yellow center

rows.label: Cinnamomum verum
rows.hook: comes from bark curled and dried into fragrant brown quills

rows.label: Coffea
rows.description: genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae
rows.hook: produces red cherries whose roasted seeds fuel the world's morning ritual
